title: Universality of a germ cocone on an etale scheme chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, and $\bar x:h_{\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}\to X$ a geometric point over $S$. Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme, $e:h_T\to X$ a representable etale map, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ an $S$-map with $e\bar t=\bar x$. Write $D_X$ for the opposite-indexed regular-function diagram on small pointed affine $X$-neighbourhoods [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models, def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model], and $D_T$ for the regular-function diagram on affine pointed etale $T$-neighbourhoods of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $c$ be a colimit cocone on $D_X$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\gamma:D_T\to\operatorname{const}(c.\mathrm{pt})$ be a natural transformation. Suppose that for every affine pointed $T$-neighbourhood $(N,\bar n)$, small pointed affine $X$-neighbourhood $(M,\bar m)$, and $S$-map $a:M\to N$ whose composite to $X$ equals the chart map of $M$ and with $a\bar m=\bar n$, the equality $\gamma_N=c_M\circ\Gamma(a)$ holds. Then the cocone with vertex $c.\mathrm{pt}$ and legs $\gamma$ is a colimit cocone. This asserts the universal property of an already specified germ cocone; it does not construct that cocone or assert an isomorphism of geometric stalk rings.

proof.text: For an arbitrary cocone d on the affine pointed T-neighbourhood diagram and a small pointed X-neighbourhood M, represent M times_X T by a scheme using the scheme test for e. Its point is the pair of the fixed geometric lift to M and t. Choose an affine open neighbourhood of that point; it is etale over T. Pull back regular functions from M to this open and use the corresponding leg of d. Any two such choices have a common pointed affine refinement; the cocone identity for d makes these composites equal. The same argument on transitions gives a cocone on ringDiagram x with vertex d.pt.

proof.text: Universality of c gives a map c.pt -> d.pt. For a T-neighbourhood N, use a compatible small refinement from lem-sfb-space-chart-germ-cocone and the pointed diagonal from N to N times_X T. Its projection equations and the assumed formula for γ show that this map composes with γ_N to d_N. For uniqueness pull each M back to T, choose an affine pointed refinement, and then a small representative. The first projection and the formula for γ identify the composite of any candidate map with c_M with the composite constructed above. Colimit hom-ext for c proves equality of any two candidates. These maps, factorization equations and uniqueness give the asserted IsColimit witness.

theorem schemeChart_germCocone_isColimit
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk s) ⟶ X.obj.obj) (T : Over S)
    (e : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.obj.obj) (he : IsEtale e)
    (t : Over.mk s ⟶ T) (ht : yoneda.map t ≫ e = x)
    (c : Cocone (ringDiagram x)) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (γ : Scheme.strictHenselizationDiagram t.left ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj c.pt)
    (hγ :
      ∀ (N : Scheme.AffinePointedEtaleNeighborhood t.left)
        (M : Neighbourhood (Over.mk s) x)
        (a : ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.left ⟶
          Over.mk (N.obj.1.hom ≫ T.hom)),
        yoneda.map (a ≫ Over.homMk N.obj.1.hom) ≫ e =
            ((neighbourhoodChart (x := x)).obj M).obj.hom →
        M.hom.left.left ≫ a.left = N.obj.2.left →
        γ.app (op N) = a.left.appTop ≫ c.ι.app (op M)) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk c.pt γ))
